```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
library(rmarkdown)
```
Tepary bean natural diversity panel is screened for early vegetative drought stress.Treatment comprises of 60% FC (Control) and 10% FC (Drought). After 14 days of sowing, plants were images (8 days) every other day throughout the experimental period. Imaging was carried out in a Raspberry pi camera. Photosynthetic measurements were measured using PhotosynQ on 13 and 16 day after sowing. Evapotranspiration measurements were measured using Arduino setup, which automatically weighs and water based on the stored reference weights.

```{r}
# Create a copy of 'spline_data' and store it in 'final_spline'

```


```{r Looping through data, fitting smoothing splines, updating data frames, and the final result}
# Loop through 'all_plants' starting from the second element (index 2) to the 586th element
for (i in 2:586) {
  # Subset 'temp' data frame for the current 'sid'
  temp <- subset(analyse, analyse$sid == all_plants[i])

  # Check if 'temp' has more than 4 rows
  if (dim(temp)[1] > 4) {
    # Fit a cubic smoothing spline to 'days' and 'Area.sum' in 'temp'
    plot.spl <- with(temp, smooth.spline(days, Area.sum, df = 4))

    # Generate predictions using the smoothing spline
    pred_temp <- predict(plot.spl, days)

    # Update specific columns in 'spline_data' with 'pred_temp' and 'temp' values
    spline_data[1:15, 4] <- pred_temp$x
    spline_data[1:15, 5] <- pred_temp$y
    spline_data[1:15, 1] <- temp$sid[1]
    spline_data[1:15, 2] <- temp$Accession[1]
    spline_data[1:15, 3] <- temp$Treatment[1]

    # Append 'spline_data' to 'final_spline'
    final_spline <- rbind(final_spline, spline_data)
  } else {
    # Set specific columns in 'spline_data' when 'temp' has <= 4 rows
    spline_data[1:15, 4] <- days
    spline_data[1:15, 5] <- 0
    spline_data[1:15, 1] <- temp$sid[1]
    spline_data[1:15, 2] <- temp$Accession[1]
    spline_data[1:15, 3] <- temp$Treatment[1]
  }
}

final_spline
```

................................. Plot for Growth rate from 7 side view images..................................................

```{r 1.Growth plot with spline fitted data}
# Convert 'Area.SUM' column to numeric type
final_spline$Area.SUM <- as.numeric(as.character(final_spline$Area.SUM))

# Convert 'day' column to a factor with numeric levels
final_spline$day <- as.factor(as.numeric(as.character(final_spline$day)))

# Create a line graph (Area_lgraph) using ggplot2
Area_lgraph <- ggplot(data = final_spline, aes(x = day, y = Area.SUM, group = ID, color = Treatment)) +

  # Add translucent lines connecting data points
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +

  # Add a ribbon indicating the mean ± SE of the data
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "ribbon", linetype = 0, aes(group = Treatment), alpha = 0.3) +

  # Add dashed lines representing the mean of the data
  stat_summary(fun = mean, aes(group = Treatment), size = 0.7, geom = "line", linetype = "dashed") +

  # Add p-values for pairwise comparisons between 'Treatment' groups
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Treatment), label = "p.signif", method = "t.test", hide.ns = TRUE) +

  # Set labels for the x and y axes
  labs(x = "Days After Stress", y = "Shoot Size (7 x SV pixels)") +

  # Customize the color scale
  scale_color_d3("category10") +

  # Adjust the legend position to the bottom
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

print(Area_lgraph)
```

# Loop it through all possible timepoints for this plant
```{r}

# Loop through each time point in 'growth_timeline'
for (t in 1:length(growth_timeline)) {
  # Define the time interval for the current time point
  min <- t - 1
  max <- min + 3

  # Subset 'temp' data frame to select rows within the time interval
  temp_now <- subset(temp, temp$day < max)
  temp_now <- subset(temp_now, temp_now$day >= min)

  # Fit a linear regression model to predict 'Area.SUM' based on 'day' for the current time interval
  model_now <- lm(temp_now$Area.SUM ~ temp_now$day)

  # Assign relevant information to 'growth_data' for the current time point
  growth_data[t, 1] <- temp_now$ID[1]
  growth_data[t, 2] <- temp_now$Accession[1]
  growth_data[t, 3] <- temp_now$Treatment[1]
  growth_data[t, 4] <- min(temp_now$day)
  growth_data[t, 5] <- model_now$coefficients[2]
}

growth_data
```

##Looping for all plants within the experiment
```{r}
# Initialize a counter to keep track of the rows in 'growth_data'
counter <- 1

# Loop through each 'ID' in 'all_plants'
for (r in 1:length(all_plants)) {
  # Subset 'final_spline' to select data for the current 'ID'
  temp <- subset(final_spline, final_spline$ID == all_plants[r])

  # Check if data for the current 'ID' exists
  if (dim(temp)[1] > 0) {
    # Loop through each time point in 'growth_timeline'
    for (t in 1:length(growth_timeline)) {
      # Define the time interval for the current time point
      min <- (t - 1)
      max <- min + 3

      # Subset 'temp' to select data within the time interval
      temp_now <- subset(temp, temp$day < max)
      temp_now <- subset(temp_now, temp_now$day >= min)

      # Check if there are enough data points in 'temp_now' for modeling
      if (dim(temp_now)[1] > 2) {
        # Fit a linear regression model to predict 'Area.SUM' based on 'day'
        model_now <- lm(temp_now$Area.SUM ~ temp_now$day)

        # Populate 'growth_data' with relevant information
        growth_data[counter, 1] <- temp_now$ID[1]
        growth_data[counter, 2] <- temp_now$Accession[1]
        growth_data[counter, 3] <- temp_now$Treatment[1]
        growth_data[counter, 4] <- min(temp_now$day)
        growth_data[counter, 5] <- model_now$coefficients[2]

        # Increment the counter
        counter <- counter + 1
      } else {
        # Increment the counter when there are not enough data points for modeling
        counter <- counter + 1
      }
    }
  }
}

# Display the dimensions of 'temp_now' (for the last iteration)
dim(temp_now)

growth_data
```

```{r}
# Create vector 'all_plants' containing unique 'ID' values from 'final_spline'
all_plants <- unique(final_spline$ID)

# Loop through each unique 'ID' in 'all_plants'
for (i in 1:length(all_plants)) {
  # Subset 'final_spline' to select data for the current 'ID'
  temp <- subset(final_spline, final_spline$ID == all_plants[i])

  # Fit a linear regression model to predict 'Area.SUM' based on 'day'
  model <- lm(temp$Area.SUM ~ temp$day)

  # Extract the growth rate (GR) coefficient from the linear regression model
  GR <- model$coefficients[2]

  # Calculate the coefficient of determination (R-squared, R2) for the model
  R2 <- summary(model)$r.squared

  # Populate 'growth_data' with relevant information for the current 'ID'
  growth_data[i, 1] <- temp$ID[1]
  growth_data[i, 2] <- temp$Accession[1]
  growth_data[i, 3] <- temp$Treatment[1]
  growth_data[i, 4] <- GR
  growth_data[i, 5] <- R2
}

growth_data
```

```{r 3. Overall Growth rate Split per treatment}
    axis.line = element_line(color = "black")
  )

GR_overall
```


```{r Stress tolerance index}
# Create a new data frame 'growth_data_clean2' containing columns 2 to 4 from 'growth_data_clean'
growth_data_clean2 <- growth_data_clean[, 2:4]

# Compute a summary of 'GR' values grouped by 'Treatment' and 'Accession' using the 'summaryBy' function
growth_sum <- summaryBy(GR ~ Treatment + Accession, data = growth_data_clean2)

growth_sum
```




```{r}
# Reshape the 'growth_sum' data frame using the 'dcast' function to create a new data frame 'growth_cast'
# where 'Accession' becomes the rows, and 'Treatment' values become columns
growth_cast <- dcast(growth_sum, Accession ~ Treatment)
```



```{r}
# Rename the second column of 'growth_cast' to 'GR.Control'
colnames(growth_cast)[2] <- "GR.Control"

# Rename the third column of 'growth_cast' to 'GR.Drought'
colnames(growth_cast)[3] <- "GR.Drought"

# Convert 'GR.Control' and 'GR.Drought' columns to numeric type
growth_cast$GR.Control <- as.numeric(as.character(growth_cast$GR.Control))
growth_cast$GR.Drought <- as.numeric(as.character(growth_cast$GR.Drought))

# Calculate the ratio of 'GR.Drought' to 'GR.Control' and store it in the 'GR.STI' column
growth_cast$GR.STI <- growth_cast$GR.Drought / growth_cast$GR.Control

growth_cast
```

```{r Load all FWDWWC excel file}
FW1 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_1.xlsx")
FW2 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_2.xlsx")
FW3 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_3.xlsx")
FW4 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_4.xlsx")
FW5 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_5.xlsx")
FW6 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_6.xlsx")
FW7 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_7.xlsx")
FW8 <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/Aparna/Desktop/ImageResults/FWDWWC_8.xlsx")
```
####### Combine all fresh weight files and write as csv file #############

```{r Bind fresh weight excel files together and saved as FW}
FW <- rbind(FW1, FW2, FW3, FW4, FW5, FW6, FW7, FW8)
write.csv(FW, "FW.csv")
```

```{r}
# Create a subset of the 'final_spline' data frame to select rows where 'day' is equal to 14
last_day <- subset(final_spline, final_spline$day == 14)
```

```{r}
# Rename second column of 'last_day' to "Accession"
colnames(last_day)[2] <- "Accession"

# Rename third column of 'last_day' to "Treatment"
colnames(last_day)[3] <- "Treatment"

# Rename fourth column of 'last_day' to "Day"
colnames(last_day)[4] <- "Day"
```

```{r}
# FW$ID <- paste0(FW$Accession, "_", substr(FW$Treatment, 1, 1))
# Create a new column 'ID' in the 'FW' data frame by concatenating values from other columns
# 'ID' is formed by combining 'Ex,' 'Accession,' and the first character of 'Treatment'

FW$ID <- paste0(FW$Ex, "_", FW$Accession, "_", substr(FW$Treatment, 1, 1))
```

```{r}
# Merge the 'last_day' and 'FW' data frames by common columns 'ID,' 'Accession,' and 'Treatment'
# Include all rows from 'last_day' (left) and 'FW' (right), filling missing values with NA

FW_lastday <- merge(last_day, FW, by = c("ID", "Accession", "Treatment"), all.x = TRUE, all.y = TRUE)
```


```{r}
# Create a subset of 'FW_lastday' data frame to select rows where 'ID' matches those in 'growth_data_clean'

clean_FW <- subset(FW_lastday, FW_lastday$ID %in% growth_data_clean$ID)

clean_FW
```

```{r}
clean_FW$FW <- as.numeric(as.character(clean_FW$FW))
clean_FW$DW <- as.numeric(as.character(clean_FW$DW))
clean_FW$WC <- as.numeric(as.character(clean_FW$WC))
```


```{r}
write.csv(clean_FW, "clean_FW.csv")
```


```{r Pearson correlation between projected shoot area and fresh weight of shoot recorded at the last day of experiment}
custom_colors <- c("lightskyblue3", "grey59")

FW_Area <- ggscatter(clean_FW, x = "FW", y = "Area.SUM", xlab = "Shoot fresh weight at 14th day (g)", ylab = "Projected shoot area (pixels)", color = "Treatment", rug = TRUE) +
  stat_cor() +
  scale_color_manual(values = custom_colors) +
  theme_minimal() # Set custom colors
FW_Area
```


```{r Pearson correlation between projected shoot area and dry weight of shoot recorded at the last day of experiment}
DW_Area <- ggscatter(clean_FW, x = "Area.SUM", y = "DW", color = "Treatment", rug = TRUE) +
  stat_cor() +
  scale_color_nejm()
DW_Area
```


```{r Pearson correlation between projected shoot area and water content (g)}
WC_Area <- ggscatter(clean_FW, x = "Area.SUM", y = "WC", color = "Treatment", rug = TRUE) +
  stat_cor() +
  scale_color_nejm()
WC_Area
```

```{r Evapotranspiration}
EVT_all <- list.files(pattern = "EVT")
EVT_all
```


```{r}
# List to store the melted data frames
melted_data <- list()

# Loop over ET1 to ET8
for (i in 1:8) {
  # Read the Excel file
  ET <- read_xlsx(EVT_all[i])

  # Remove the first column
  ET <- ET %>% select(-1)

  # Melt the data
  ET_melted <- melt(ET, id.vars = c("PotTag", "Accession", "Treatment"))

  # Rename the columns
  colnames(ET_melted)[4] <- "day"
  colnames(ET_melted)[5] <- "ET"

  # Modify the 'day' coloumn
  ET_melted$day <- gsub("Day", "", ET_melted$day)

  # Add the 'exp' column
  ET_melted <- ET_melted %>%
    mutate(exp = i)

  # Store the melted data frame in the list
  melted_data[[i]] <- ET_melted
}

# Merge the melted data frames
merged_data <- bind_rows(melted_data)

# Find the unique 'day' values
unique_days <- merged_data %>%
  group_by(exp) %>%
  distinct(day, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  select(exp, day)
```


```{r 4.Evapotranspiration (g water/day) after days of stress---Without smooth spline}
# Convert the 'ET' column in 'merged_data' to numeric type
merged_data$ET <- as.numeric(as.character(merged_data$ET))

# merged_data$ID <- paste(merged_data$exp, merged_data$PotTag, merged_data$Accession, merged_data$Treatment, sep="_")

# Create a unique 'ID' by concatenating values from 'exp,' 'Accession,' and the first character of 'Treatment'
merged_data$ID <- paste(merged_data$exp, merged_data$Accession, substr(merged_data$Treatment, 1, 1), sep = "_")

# Rename the fifth column of 'merged_data' to "EVT"
colnames(merged_data)[5] <- "EVT"

# Create a subset 'ET_clean' of 'merged_data' where 'EVT' is greater than 0, less than 200, and 'day' is less than 15
ET_clean <- subset(merged_data, merged_data$EVT > 0)
ET_clean <- subset(ET_clean, ET_clean$EVT < 200)
ET_clean$day <- as.numeric(ET_clean$day)

# Convert the 'day' column in 'ET_clean' to a factor
ET_clean$day <- as.factor(as.numeric(as.character(ET_clean$day)))

# Create a line graph 'ET_lgraph' using 'ET_clean' data for visualization
ET_lgraph <- ggplot(data = ET_clean, aes(x = day, y = EVT, group = ID, color = Treatment)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.1) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = mean_se, geom = "ribbon", linetype = 0, aes(group = Treatment), alpha = 0.3) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, aes(group = Treatment), size = 0.7, geom = "line", linetype = "dashed") +
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Treatment), label = "p.signif", method = "t.test", hide.ns = TRUE) +
  ylab("Evapotranspiration (g H2O / day)") +
  xlab("Days After Stress") +
  scale_color_d3()

ET_lgraph
```


```{r Smooth splines for Evapotranspiration}
# Create a vector 'days' representing a range from 1 to 14
days <- 1:14

# Create a subset 'temp' of the 'ET_clean' data frame for the first unique 'ID'
temp <- subset(ET_clean, ET_clean$ID == unique(ET_clean$ID)[1])

# Convert the 'day' column in 'temp' to numeric type
temp$day <- as.numeric(as.character(temp$day))

temp$day
```

```{r}
temp$EVT
```

```{r}
# Fit a cubic smoothing spline ('smooth.spline') to the 'day' and 'EVT' data in 'temp'
plot.spl <- with(temp, smooth.spline(day, EVT, df = 5))

# Create a scatter plot of 'EVT' against 'day' using data from 'temp'
plot(EVT ~ day, data = temp)

# Add a blue line representing the cubic smoothing spline to the scatter plot
lines(plot.spl, col = "blue")

# Add a red line representing the predicted values from the cubic smoothing spline for the 'days' vector
lines(predict(plot.spl, days), col = "red")
```


```{r}
# Create a vector 'names' specifying column names for a new data frame 'EVT_spline_data'
names <- c(text = "ID", "Accession", "Treatment", "day", "EVT")

# Create an empty data frame 'EVT_spline_data' with columns set as character vectors
EVT_spline_data <- data.frame()
for (k in names) EVT_spline_data[[k]] <- as.character()

EVT_spline_data
```


```{r}
# Generate predictions for 'EVT' using the cubic smoothing spline model 'plot.spl' and the 'days' vector
pred_temp <- predict(plot.spl, days)
pred_temp
```


```{r}
# Populate the 'EVT_spline_data' data frame with predictions from 'pred_temp' and other information
# Rows 1 to 14 are assigned 'pred_temp$x' values to the 4th column and 'pred_temp$y' values to the 5th column
# First three columns receive values from the corresponding columns in the 'temp' data
EVT_spline_data[1:14, 4] <- pred_temp$x
EVT_spline_data[1:14, 5] <- pred_temp$y
EVT_spline_data[1:14, 1] <- temp$ID[1]
EVT_spline_data[1:14, 2] <- temp$Accession[1]
EVT_spline_data[1:14, 3] <- temp$Treatment[1]

EVT_spline_data
```

```{r}
# Create a 'EVT_spline_data' data frame as 'final_EVT_spline'
final_EVT_spline <- EVT_spline_data

# Extract unique 'ID' values from 'ET_clean' and calculate the length
all_plants <- unique(ET_clean$ID)
length(all_plants)
```

```{r looping through the data}
# Loop through unique 'ID' values starting from the second one (index 2) to the 609th
for (i in 2:609) {
  # Create a subset 'temp' of 'ET_clean' for the current 'ID'
  temp <- subset(ET_clean, ET_clean$ID == all_plants[i])

  # Check if the number of rows in 'temp' is greater than 4
  if (dim(temp)[1] > 4) {
    # Fit a cubic smoothing spline to the 'day' and 'EVT' data in 'temp'
    plot.spl <- with(temp, smooth.spline(day, EVT, df = 5))

    # Generate predictions for 'EVT' using the smoothing spline and 'days'
    pred_temp <- predict(plot.spl, days)

    # Update the first 14 rows of 'EVT_spline_data' with predictions and other information
    EVT_spline_data[1:14, 4] <- pred_temp$x
    EVT_spline_data[1:14, 5] <- pred_temp$y
    EVT_spline_data[1:14, 1] <- temp$ID[1]
    EVT_spline_data[1:14, 2] <- temp$Accession[1]
    EVT_spline_data[1:14, 3] <- temp$Treatment[1]

    # Append the updated 'EVT_spline_data' to 'final_EVT_spline'
    final_EVT_spline <- rbind(final_EVT_spline, EVT_spline_data)
  } else {
    # For 'temp' with fewer than 5 rows, set specific values in 'spline_data'
    spline_data[1:14, 4] <- days
    spline_data[1:14, 5] <- 0
    spline_data[1:14, 1] <- temp$ID[1]
    spline_data[1:14, 2] <- temp$Accession[1]
    spline_data[1:14, 3] <- temp$Treatment[1]
  }
}

final_EVT_spline
```

```{r}
#Fm Paired
# Define custom colors for the plot
custom_colors <- c("lightskyblue3", "gray59")

# Create a ggplot2 plot for FoPrime data in 'cPSQ' data frame
Fm_paired <- ggplot(data = cPSQ, mapping = aes(x = Treatment, y = FmPrime, fill = Treatment)) +

  # Add a line plot with grouping by 'Accession', with some transparency (alpha = 0.1)
  geom_line(mapping = aes(group = Accession), alpha = 0.1, position = position_dodge(0.1)) +

  # Add a violin plot overlaid with individual data points (dots)
  geom_violindot(dots_size = 0.08, position_dots = position_dodge(0.1), flip = c(1)) +

  # Add individual data points (as filled circles)
  geom_point(mapping = aes(fill = Treatment, group = Accession), size = 1.5, shape = 21, position = position_dodge(0.1)) +

  # Add statistical comparison annotations (p-values) between treatment groups using ANOVA
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Treatment), label = "p.signif", method = "aov", hide.ns = TRUE) +

  # Set the plot theme to a white background
  theme_bw() +

  # Set custom fill colors for the 'Treatment' variable
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +

  # Remove the legend
  theme(legend.position = "none") +

  # Label the y-axis and remove the x-axis label
  ylab("FmPrime") +
  xlab("")

Fm_paired
```

```{r }
#Fo Prime_Paired

# Define custom colors for the plot
custom_colors <- c("lightskyblue3", "gray59")

# Create a ggplot2 plot for FoPrime data in 'cPSQ' data frame
FoPrime_plot_paired <- ggplot(data = cPSQ, mapping = aes(x = Treatment, y = FoPrime, fill = Treatment)) +

  # Add a line plot with grouping by 'Accession', with some transparency (alpha = 0.1)
  geom_line(mapping = aes(group = Accession), alpha = 0.1, position = position_dodge(0.1)) +

  # Add a violin plot overlaid with individual data points (dots)
  geom_violindot(dots_size = 0.08, position_dots = position_dodge(0.1), flip = c(1)) +

  # Add individual data points (as filled circles)
  geom_point(mapping = aes(fill = Treatment, group = Accession), size = 1.5, shape = 21, position = position_dodge(0.1)) +

  # Add statistical comparison annotations (p-values) between treatment groups using ANOVA
  stat_compare_means(aes(group = Treatment), label = "p.signif", method = "aov", hide.ns = TRUE) +

  # Set the plot theme to a white background
  theme_bw() +

  # Set custom fill colors for the 'Treatment' variable
  scale_fill_manual(values = custom_colors) +

  # Remove the legend
  theme(legend.position = "none") +

  # Label the y-axis and remove the x-axis label
  ylab("FoPrime") +
  xlab("")

FoPrime_plot_paired
```

```{r Regression Analysis}
# Initialize empty matrices for regression statistics
reg.Adj.Rsq <- matrix(, nrow = 24, ncol = 24) # Matrix for adjusted R-squared values
reg.Rsq <- matrix(, nrow = 24, ncol = 24) # Matrix for R-squared values
reg.pval <- matrix(, nrow = 24, ncol = 24) # Matrix for p-values
reg.RSE <- matrix(, nrow = 24, ncol = 24) # Matrix for residual standard errors
reg.DF = matrix(, nrow = 24, ncol = 24)   # Matrix for degrees of freedom

# Set column and row names for reg.Rsq matrix based on sel_traits_reg
colnames(reg.Rsq) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)
rownames(reg.Rsq) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)

# Set column and row names for reg.Adj.Rsq matrix based on sel_traits_reg
colnames(reg.Adj.Rsq) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)
rownames(reg.Adj.Rsq) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)

# Set column and row names for reg.pval matrix based on sel_traits_reg
colnames(reg.pval) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)
rownames(reg.pval) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)

# Set column and row names for reg.RSE matrix based on sel_traits_reg
colnames(reg.RSE) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)
rownames(reg.RSE) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)

# Set column and row names for reg.DF matrix based on sel_traits_reg
colnames(reg.DF) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)
rownames(reg.DF) <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)
```


```{r}
# I want to explain each trait -- colnames(sel_traits_reg)[1:38] -- by each trait -- colnames(sel_traits_reg)[1:38]
# Loop through 24 traits as both dependent and independent variables
for (x in 1:24) {
  trait.y <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)[x] # Get the name of the dependent variable (trait.y)

  # Nested loop for the independent variable (trait.x)
  for (y in 1:24) {
    trait.x <- colnames(sel_traits_reg)[y] # Get the name of the independent variable (trait.x)

    # Perform linear regression and store the results in the matrices
    reg.Adj.Rsq[y - 1, x - 1] <- summary(lm(paste(trait.y, "~", trait.x), data = sel_traits_reg))$adj.r.squared
    reg.Rsq[y - 1, x - 1] <- summary(lm(paste(trait.y, "~", trait.x), data = sel_traits_reg))$r.squared

    # Extract p-value for the coefficient of trait.x
    pval_table <- summary(lm(paste(trait.y, "~", trait.x), data = sel_traits_reg))$coefficients
    if (dim(pval_table)[1] > 1) {
      reg.pval[y - 1, x - 1] <- summary(lm(paste(trait.y, "~", trait.x), data = sel_traits_reg))$coefficients[2, 4]
    } else {
      reg.pval[y - 1, x - 1] <- "N.A." # Set "N.A." if there's no second coefficient
    }

    # Store residual standard error
    reg.RSE[y - 1, x - 1] <- summary(lm(paste(trait.y, "~", trait.x), data = sel_traits_reg))$sigma
  }
}

# After running this code snippet the matrices reg.Adj.Rsq, reg.Rsq, reg.pval, and reg.RSE contain regression statistics for all pairs of traits.
```


```{r}
# Loop through all combinations of traits in the matrices
for (x in 1:24) {
  for (y in 1:24) {
    # Check if reg.pval[x, y] is not missing (NA) and if it's either "N.A." or greater than 0.01
    if (!is.na(reg.pval[x, y]) && (reg.pval[x, y] == "N.A." || as.numeric(reg.pval[x, y]) > 0.01)) {
      # If the condition is met (p-value is not significant):

      # Set reg.Adj.Rsq and reg.Rsq at this position to NA
      reg.Adj.Rsq[x, y] <- NA
      reg.Rsq[x, y] <- NA
    } else {
      # If the condition is not met (p-value is significant):

      # Convert and assign the numeric values from reg.Adj.Rsq and reg.Rsq
      reg.Adj.Rsq[x, y] <- as.numeric(reg.Adj.Rsq[x, y])
      reg.Rsq[x, y] <- as.numeric(reg.Rsq[x, y])
    }
  }
}
```
